name: Everyday Things
blurb: Familiar finds from the junk drawer to the driveway

clues: I make tall people feel like a home improvement project.
You can take me shopping for furniture.
I have a tiny metal hook.
I spring back into a case.
Pull out my numbered ribbon to find the width of a doorway.
I ruin the confidence of whoever checks the forecast.
Wind is my worst enemy.
I spend sunny days folded up.
A set of ribs spreads my fabric overhead.
You open me on the sidewalk to stay dry in a downpour.
I have a terrible record of keeping things to myself.
I often sit in the sink.
Many small holes cover my bowl.
I keep dinner from going down the drain.
Tip cooked pasta into me to let the boiling water run away.
I bring things together by stabbing them.
I belong in a desk drawer.
My supplies arrive in shiny strips.
Pressing my top bends two tiny metal legs.
I fasten a stack of pages at one corner.
I have one job and it involves getting in the way.
I spend most of my day on the floor.
I can be triangular and rubbery.
Shove me under the edge of something that swings.
I keep an open entrance from swinging shut.
I spend a lot of time getting punched by tired people.
People disagree about how firm I should be.
Hotel beds have more of me than anyone needs.
A washable case fits over me.
You put your head on me to fall asleep.
I have a two-minute workday and still get replaced.
I often stand in a cup.
Mine come with manual or electric handles.
Paste goes on my bristles.
You scrub your molars with me before bed.
I have two legs and never go for walks.
Craft projects leave me sticky.

Two loops fit your fingers so you can cut paper.
I turn strangers into people who stare silently at a number.
My music has a reputation.
I have a maximum weight.
You might hold my doors for a late arrival.
I carry you vertically between floors without stairs.
I am a bank for loose change that pays no interest.
Moving me can turn friends into enemies.
People choose sides on me without thinking about it.
My cushions are suspiciously good at collecting crumbs.
Several people sit on me to watch TV.
I quietly judge people who buy things they never finish.
You might have to anchor me to a wall.
Some people organize my contents by color.
I have a row of shelves above another row of shelves.
Novels and reference volumes stand upright on me.
My repairs are often described as temporary for years.
I am popular in garages and backstage.
You can tear a piece of me without tools.
My silver-gray strips are sticky underneath and reinforced with fabric.
I come on a roll and patch almost anything in an emergency.
People only find me after they need me.
I often live near spare batteries.
Camping is one of my better gigs.
My beam points wherever you aim my handle.
You carry me to see during a blackout.
I make falling down more likely immediately after helping.
I have a surprisingly wet hairdo.
I work with a bucket.
Mine can be made of string or a flat pad.
I clean hard floors from the end of a long handle.
I do my best work when absolutely soaked.
I often sit next to a sink.
You can squeeze me dry with one hand.
One side might be rougher than the other.
I soak up suds for washing dishes by hand.
A household can feud over me without anyone saying a word.
I usually live on an inside wall.
Some versions learn when you're usually home.
I show a number people keep nudging up or down.
I tell the heating or cooling system what indoor temperature to maintain.
My worst time to break is right before a picture.
I am found on tents as well as clothes.
I have teeth and a little tab.
Sliding that tab joins two rows together.
I close the front of a jacket in one pull.
I have strong feelings about being left unattended.
I might have a cord or sit on a burner.
I have a handle and a pouring spout.
Some versions whistle when they are ready.
I heat water for a mug of tea.
I know exactly how much your pet contributes to your wardrobe.
I am handy before a job interview.
My surface stops helping once it looks furry.
You peel off my dirty outer sheet.
I roll sticky paper over clothes to pick up stray hairs.
I am proof that the nearest wall is never close enough.
People trip over me at parties.
I coil up when I'm off duty.
I have a plug on one end and a socket on the other.
I bring electricity to a device whose cable won't reach the outlet.
I make waiting for breakfast unnecessarily suspenseful.
I accumulate crumbs you can shake out.
My lever stays down while I work.
There are usually two narrow slots on top.
I pop up warm browned slices of bread.
I make being lazy look adventurous.
I am hard to share gracefully.
I can be made of rope or cloth.
I hang between two supports.
You lie in my sagging middle for a nap between trees.
I can only make progress by losing something.
I spend half my time upside down.
People sometimes play board games with me.
My two clear chambers meet in a narrow neck.
Sand trickles from my upper bulb to measure a fixed interval.
Every step I take is also a step I lose.
A second person sometimes holds my feet.
I can fold or lean.
My rungs give you places to stand.
You climb me to reach the roof.
I get both love letters and coupons with the same expression.
A little flag can stick up from my side.
Some of me stand by the curb.
There is usually a hinged door to check.
A postal worker puts envelopes addressed to you inside me.
You see me when breakfast requires a little stunt.
Too much heat can melt my cheaper cousins.
My broad end is flat and thin.
I can slip under a pancake.
You lift me by the handle to flip a burger in a pan.
I destroy a little of what I fix.
A tiny version can live in a schoolbag.
Sometimes there's a crank.
I collect curled shavings.

I fix wardrobe emergencies by making new holes.
I can be smaller than a fingernail.
My bent metal acts like a spring.
The clasp covers my pointed end.
I temporarily fasten two pieces of fabric without sewing them.
I am useless on the floor and still end up there.
I can be velvet, plastic or wire.
I have shoulders and no head.
A hook rests over the closet rod.
A shirt keeps its shape while dangling from me.
I am sometimes opened to great applause.
I can keep a room cooler.
I often come as a pair.
My fabric slides along a rod.
Close me across a window for privacy or darkness.
I specialize in scenes of tiny wet crimes.
I am often rectangular and fluffy.
A grippy bottom helps me stay put.
People step on me with dripping feet.
I soak up water beside the tub or shower.
I specialize in tiny renovations that take hours.
People walk very slowly when carrying me full.
Sometimes you twist me to make me let go.
I have a grid of little compartments.
Fill me with water and freeze me to make cubes for drinks.
I make a dignified person look like a mushroom.
Hotels sometimes leave me in a wrapper.
My outer edge is elastic.
The plastic covers most of your hair.
Put me over your head before rinsing off to keep your hair dry.
I flatten people’s problems if their problems are dough.
My wooden version feels surprisingly heavy.
I sometimes wear a light coat of flour.
Grab me at both ends and move me back and forth.
I turn a lump of pastry into an even sheet.
I am good at holding groups together under tension.
I have been fired across more than one classroom.
I stretch and snap back.
I am shaped like an elastic loop.
Wrap me around a bundle of pencils to hold them together.
People regularly ask me questions I can't answer.
A lot of what I receive is empty.
I might be blue or green.
A triangle of arrows often marks me.
I collect sorted cans, cardboard or bottles instead of ordinary garbage.
I have attended more meetings than my owner.
My handle gives me a distinctive silhouette.
I can display a joke no coworker asked to read.
I'm usually made of ceramic.
I hold your morning coffee while my handle keeps your fingers off the hot sides.
I do my networking at baggage claim.
Most days I sit in a closet.
You can buy one in a color that stands out.
I attach to the handle of a suitcase.
Find my card to read the owner's contact details.
I am elbowed around all day and somehow one wheel is always my fault.
I often have a seat for a small child.
I can nest tightly into others of my kind.
My basket runs on four wheels.
You push me around a supermarket and unload groceries at checkout.
I have a reputation for being polite while getting stepped on.
I make it easy to guess who came in with muddy shoes.
My lettering tends to wear out.
You find me outside a front entrance.
Wipe the soles of your shoes on me before ringing the bell.
I frequently lose my closest friend to the laundry.
My nicer versions are given as disappointing gifts.
I might be rolled into a small ball.
I cover toes but usually stay hidden beneath shoes.
You pull one stretchy tube onto each foot.
I often arrive just before someone says they're fine.
I am a fixture in waiting rooms.
Mine can be decorated to match a room.
Pulling one thin sheet makes another stick out of my opening.
I dispense disposable paper for noses and tears.
I can save a friendship on a camping trip.
I usually come as two tiny pieces.
One kind is squishy foam.
Push me into place before a loud concert.
I block some of the sound before it reaches your inner hearing.
I have one useful finger and a very brave job.
I lie around the kitchen between emergencies.
I often hang from a loop.
My thick fabric keeps heat from reaching a hand.
Wear me to lift a hot baking sheet.
I can make a person look official in an instant.
I am popular with people walking around taking notes.
I offer a surface to write on while standing.
A spring-loaded clamp grips my top edge.
I hold a sheet of paper flat on a stiff board.
The louder I am, the more likely someone is overloading me.
I spend almost all day next to the sink.
I keep several plates on their edges.
Some versions drain into a tray.
Put wet bowls and glasses on me after washing them by hand.
I only fly in very specific circumstances.
I help you avoid bending over several times.
A small pan usually follows my work.
I have stiff bristles on a long pole.
Sweep crumbs across the floor with me.
I protect a surface from evidence of good hospitality.
People who own me notice when I am ignored.
I could be made from cork or cardboard.
I am only a little bigger than the base of a glass.
Put me under a drink to keep wet rings off the coffee table.
I make a car feel like it has permission to come home.
I tend to live clipped above the driver.
Mine needs a battery.
A button sends a signal from the driveway.
I tell the big motorized door where you park to open or close.
Some people spend an entire afternoon smelling me before taking one home.
A birthday is suddenly quieter after I'm used.
I get shorter while I work.
A small wick runs through my wax.
Light me with a match for a little flame.
I hand out a very strict allowance.
I often live by a sink.
Some versions have a sensor so you never touch them.
Mine often has a downward pump and a short nozzle.
Press me once to get liquid cleanser for your hands.
I prevent neglect with a surprisingly jaunty silhouette.
I am often carried in one hand.
My spout may end in a cap full of holes.
I imitate rain on a small scale.
Bring me to a houseplant to give the soil a drink.
My success makes everyone immediately look away.
You might store me near a window.
I often have a floppy grid on a long handle.
I require faster reactions than my target expects.
Swing me to smack a buzzing insect against a wall.
I'm flat enough for my job and oddly pointy about it.
My legs often fold into an X.
My cover is padded and fits tightly.
A shirt can wrap around my narrow end.
I support clothing while heat and pressure remove its wrinkles.
I shuttle between two rooms and get blamed when clothes vanish.
My walls often have holes.
There are usually handles on two sides.
I can be heaped with either clean or dirty clothes.
Carry me to the washer when the hamper is full.
People usually shout over me and hope it helps.
I get loudest right before breakfast.
A lid stops my mess becoming everyone’s problem.
My fast blade sits near the bottom of a pitcher.
I turn frozen fruit and milk into a smoothie.
I keep a polite distance from everything I touch.
I come in handy when someone drops food into a deep pan.
My ends may be scalloped or covered with silicone.
Squeezing my handles brings my two jaws together.
Use me to grab salad or turn sizzling sausages on a grill.
I am usually complimented for what someone put inside me.
I may stand on a table or hang on a wall.
I have a clear front over a removable backing.
I add a border around a favorite image.
Put a family photo behind my glass to display it.
I perform better when someone loses their patience.

I beat air into egg whites.
I mix batter quickly by hand without using a spoon.
I am the reason a bake-off stops being improvisational.
